analysis.title: Global Reflections - 7 Nov 2026 (Nick Savone, Institutional Equity Division)
key_insights: Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth is tracking 31.4% with 84% of reporting companies beating EPS, but the aggregate beat is only 2.7%, below recent averages. Revisions breadth has eased to +10% from a +26% peak.

FCF surprises are driving larger stock reactions than EPS surprises. The debate has shifted to AI spending in 2028. PLTR revenue growth reached 96% YoY for a 13th straight quarter of acceleration with a muted reaction, and SHOP fell sharply despite 30% constant-currency GMV growth.

Wednesday's 1.6% S&P 500 gain reversed on Thursday with a 6.4% Nasdaq 100 decline and 12.2% SOX fall. For the week the S&P 500 fell 2.7% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 4.9%. The Nasdaq 100 drop was its worst day since March 2020 and the 4th worst in 15 years.

The US TMT Momentum pair is down 70% from June highs, its largest one-year drawdown on record. The Global Risk Demand Index hit -3.4SD, its lowest in over a year. 60% of Russell 3000 stocks had corrected at least 20% since June before Thursday.

Hedge funds de-risked further into the midterm relief rally. US L/S net leverage fell 5% on Thursday (5th largest one-day decline on record) and 8ppts on the week to 42%. Gross fell 4ppts to 202%, a 12-month low. AI exposure is ~32% of US net exposure vs 47% at the June peak.

October payrolls rose 165K vs 70K expected and unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Markets price fewer than two Fed hikes through end-2027, down from 3-4 a month ago, and a December hike remains in discussion. Slowing wage growth eases overheating concerns.

Asia sold off Friday: KOSPI 200 fell 6.5% with a circuit breaker triggered on the broader KOSPI, the Nikkei fell 6.0% and TOPIX 5.9%. China was more resilient, with the Hang Seng down 1.3% and HSTECH down 1.8%.

Europe was roughly flat on the week. STOXX 600 rose 1.8% Wednesday and fell 0.4% Thursday. ASML fell 6.5% and Infineon 8.5% on AI rollout concerns. Brent fell nearly 20% over three sessions through Wednesday and French 10Y yields fell almost 18bps on Wednesday.

Stephen Byrd sees growing opposition to data center development after the midterms, raising the risk of US power shortages. ERCOT's interconnection queue is ~474GW, more than 5x peak demand. Texas-exposed CIFR, GLXY and SEI face uncertainty, while WMB, EQIX, DLR and BE could benefit.
Previous 6%+ Nasdaq down days over the last 15Y were all followed by Nasdaq gains of more than 25% over 3M and at least 40% over 6M.

MS Matthew Cost is bullish on APP after 3Q revenue and EBITDA beat MS estimates by 5% and 6%. Gaming ad revenue grew ~50% YoY and ecommerce ad revenue grew over 100% YoY. 4Q revenue is expected to grow ~8% QoQ.

MRVL announced an all-stock acquisition of LITE at ~$115B EV. Joe Moore sees a strong technology rationale but flags concerns about MRVL's neutral-supplier position and execution risk. He thinks the MRVL selloff is overdone.

Lee Simpson says the 7% ASML selloff is overdone, with the valuation implying a 20% cut to consensus 2028 EPS. MS reiterates ASML as an Overweight Top Pick with a EUR1,700 PT. European Semis trade at a 19% P/E discount to Software vs a 116% premium at the highs.

Mike Wilson thinks the correction is in its final innings and is waiting for more capitulation or a move to 7,100-7,300 before adding risk more aggressively. He keeps an 8,000 year-end base case and prefers durable FCF and quality cyclicals, particularly Industrials.

Michael Gapen estimates AI-related spending added 0.9ppts to annualized 3Q GDP growth, vs 0.5ppts in 2025. He keeps a $1.6T hyperscaler capex outlook for 2027 and expects two 25bps Fed hikes in December and March.

Ariana Salvatore expects Democrats' sweep to delay SNAP and Medicaid cuts, adding up to 0.4ppts to 2027 consumption. She flags state-level data center restrictions as a near-term headwind for AI sentiment.
Euro area headline inflation rose to 4.0% YoY in October with core at 2.5%. Excess liquidity is approaching EUR2T. MS expects no imminent change to ECB reserve requirements.

China October manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 from 50.1. Chief China Equity Strategist Laura Wang sees selective entry points in oversold, fundamentally sound equities while keeping a cautious broader market stance.
Takeshi Yamaguchi warns that persistent equity volatility could delay the BoJ's December hike to January. The BoJ plans to accelerate ETF sales in January 2027.
Joyce Jiang finds 16% of leveraged loan software debt is high AI-disruption risk, 49% moderate and 35% low. Nearly 3/4 of the high-risk exposure is rated B-/CCC. CLOs hold 12% high-risk exposure.
Martijn Rats returns to a $75/bbl Brent forecast by 4Q27 and keeps 1Q27 at $100/bbl. He moves Equinor and OMV to Underweight, stays In-Line on the sector, and keeps BP as Top Pick.
MS issued several rating changes this week. Upgrades: Yamaha, Cinemark and Acadian to OW. Downgrades: Coinbase to UW, Cisco to EW and Camtek to UW. It also initiated PONY and Huaqin at OW.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth tracking 31.4% (FactSet-style aggregate). 84% of reporting companies beat EPS vs 82% one-year average and 78% five-year average. Aggregate beat is 2.7%. 74% beat consensus sales vs 77% one-year average and 70% five-year average. 88% of S&P 500 companies have reported.
PLTR reported 3Q revenue growth of 96% YoY, its 13th consecutive quarter of acceleration, with a muted stock reaction. SHOP fell sharply despite 30% constant-currency GMV growth.
AAPL reported 17% iPhone growth but slowing Services and margin pressure from memory inflation and AI costs. AMD offset PC weakness with stronger server CPU expectations.
NET reported revenue growth accelerating to 39% from 36% last quarter. ABNB reported 16% room-night growth vs approximately 12% expected.
APP 3Q (reported): revenue beat MS estimates by 5% and EBITDA beat by 6%. MS expects 4Q revenue to grow ~8% QoQ.
Sony 2Q operating profit reported at JPY622bn vs JPY491bn consensus, with FY guidance raised. Toyota raised its FY operating profit forecast to JPY3.9tn vs JPY3.8tn consensus.
Nintendo reported solid Software sales offset by slower Switch 2 hardware demand after the price increase. FY guidance is unchanged.

Ferrari raised FY26 guidance for a second time this year after 10.9% price/mix growth. Rheinmetall fell 16% after cutting its sales outlook again. Maersk fell 6% despite raising guidance. Diageo rose 3% on unexpected organic sales growth.
Only 13% of S&P market cap reported this week, with ~14% still to report. The earnings revisions breadth (ERB) is at +10% vs a +26% peak.
AAMI 3Q flows missed on timing. MS projects ~8% organic growth, 14% revenue and 18% ENI EPS CAGRs through 2028.
CSCO downgraded ahead of FQ1 results. MS sees few chances to exceed full expectations.
MS European Research previews an earnings week focused on whether resilient pricing and cost discipline can offset uneven volumes.

risk_factors: Further de-grossing and systematic selling after the Nasdaq's worst day since March 2020.
AI financing and returns concerns, with 2028 AI spending as the focus of the debate.
State-level data center restrictions, particularly in Texas, and local opposition, which could delay new projects. About 5 GW is at risk of delay in '28 per Cam McVeigh.
A stronger economy could keep the Fed hiking. A December hike remains in the discussion.
A deeper equity decline could tighten financial conditions. It could delay the BoJ's December hike to January.
France's unresolved fiscal and political uncertainty.
AI disruption risk in leveraged software loans, with 16% classified as high risk.
MRVL's execution risk and neutral-supplier concerns after the LITE acquisition.
Crypto backdrop uncertainty after the recent Binance hack.
Euro area inflation at 4.0% headline with further price pressures expected.
vol_and_positioning: The Nasdaq VIX hit its highest level since Liberation Day. Single-name volatility on S&P 500 names over the last 2 weeks is in the 99th percentile vs the last 5 years (+16 percentile points WoW).

1M dispersion in US stock returns is in the 99th percentile of the 20Y range, matching Covid-era highs and only exceeded in the GFC. EU 1M dispersion is in the 96th percentile, the highest since March 2022.

US L/S net leverage fell 5% on Thursday, the 5th largest daily decline on record, to 42%, the lowest decile historically. Bottom-decile net leverage has historically been followed by positive S&P forward returns.
US L/S gross leverage fell 4ppts to 202% (87th percentile since 2010, 0th percentile over 1Y), a 12-month low. Cumulative L/S de-grossing since June is ~10.7% of global GMV.
SOX had its 2nd worst day ever and trades on a single-digit 2Y forward P/E for the first time in 5 years. The worst day was March 2020.
Global Risk Demand reached deep fear territory, the 7th drop from neutral to fear in the last two months.
Retail's heavy opening sales on Thursday reversed as ETF demand left the group net buyers by the close. Systematic selling remains a headwind.
MS offers the Defensive Portfolio (MSCBCDF0), a systematic tail-hedging strategy through a TRS swap, designed to provide continuous protection against major selloffs.
S&P 500 dispersion in the last 2w is in the 60th percentile vs 5Y. The ratio of between-sector to within-sector dispersion is in the 81st percentile.
geopolitical: Middle East resolution looks more likely but is not imminent, per Martijn Rats. Brent fell nearly 20% over three sessions through Wednesday.
The US midterms delivered a Democratic sweep of Congress. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's win and Ohio's election raise data center permitting concerns.
Executive-led tariff and geopolitical policies are expected to persist, per Ariana Salvatore.
France's fiscal and political uncertainty remains unresolved.
US dispersion remains fractionally below levels reached in April around the early stages of the US-Iran conflict.
Reports suggest Japan may use BoJ ETF sale gains to fund a new economic-security account.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is much lighter, with L/S net leverage at 42% (lowest decile) and still-positive earnings revisions. Bottom-decile net leverage has historically been followed by positive S&P returns, and past 6%+ Nasdaq drops were followed by large 3M gains.
tension_points.bear_case: Wednesday's relief was used to cut exposure further rather than rebuild. About 40% of US L/S funds are flat or down YTD, systematic selling remains a headwind, and confidence does not reset as neatly as exposure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rebound that is only shorts covering rather than longs being rebuilt, or a CPI print next week that keeps the rates debate unresolved.

tension_points.bull_case: Slowing wage growth eases overheating concerns, and a softer CPI next week could ease the rates debate. Market pricing of hikes fell to fewer than two from 3-4.
tension_points.bear_case: Payrolls of 165K vs 70K expected, strong 3Q GDP and firm data keep a December hike in the discussion. MS economics expects hikes in December and March.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's CPI print is the immediate test. A softer print would ease the rates debate.

tension_points.bull_case: Projects under construction are expected to be insulated, and the $1.6T 2027 hyperscaler capex outlook is intact. AI added 0.9ppts to 3Q GDP growth.
tension_points.bear_case: State-level data center restrictions, particularly in Texas, plus energy costs and local opposition, add permitting risk. About 5 GW is at risk of delay in '28 and the debate has moved to 2028 AI spending.

tension_points.bull_case: Semis trade at a 19% P/E discount to Software vs a 116% premium at the highs. ASML's valuation implies a 20% cut to consensus 2028 EPS.
tension_points.bear_case: AI rollout concerns pressured ASML (-6.5%) and Infineon (-8.5%), and momentum has fallen more than 20% since June.

tension_points.bull_case: Mike Wilson sees the correction in its final innings, with breadth improving and the equal-weighted S&P outperforming by nearly 6% since September.
tension_points.bear_case: Systematic selling persists and Fed policy and geopolitical risks remain. Wilson himself awaits further capitulation before adding risk aggressively.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wilson waits for further capitulation or a move toward 7,100-7,300 on the S&P 500 before adding risk more aggressively.
